summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.
